first.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing is the most acute and time-sensitive threat, directly targeting price-sensitive SMB accounts—the same segment memory_73 covers. That memory shows promotional pricing lifted acquisition/revenue and even cut time-to-first-value, which could indirectly help the activation and onboarding metrics too, making it the most leveraged single bet given only one experimental slot. I verify memory_73 because it's the evidence base for the chosen action and because pricing moves carry real margin/long-term revenue risk that must be checked against the original experiment's actual conditions (was it a discount, tiered plan, time-limited promo, etc.) rather than the summarized takeaway. I also verify memory_31 (onboarding simplification) as the strongest competing hypothesis, since onboarding completion is currently down and a low-risk funnel fix could be safer, so I want to confirm its original effect size and durability before ruling it out. Importantly, memory_73's prior success occurred without an active competitor price war; matching or undercutting a competitor now is a materially different causal context (risk of margin erosion, race-to-bottom, or attracting low-LTV switchers) that the archived record won't have tested, so I'm keeping this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout and flagging downstream value risk explicitly. I'm not treating memory_73's historical lift as a guarantee under the new competitive dynamic—only as directionally supportive evidence.
